figures.title: An engine is one part of the Node runtime
figures.description: Application JavaScript executes in V8 and calls Node host APIs. Those APIs connect to operation-specific native and OS facilities. V8 execution and host facilities are distinct responsibilities.

figures.title: Two different bases for a resource path
figures.description: A relative filesystem path uses the process working directory. A URL constructed from import.meta.url uses the module location. Changing cwd changes only the former base in this example.

figures.title: Entry context changes the queue relationship
figures.description: Both entries print sync-start then sync-end. The CJS entry next runs nextTick, promise, microtask. The ESM entry instead runs promise, microtask, nextTick. These are separate fixture contexts.

figures.title: emit returns before an async listener completes
figures.description: In await mode emit invokes the async listener through async-start and suspension, then invokes the second listener and returns true. The async listener later resumes and prints async-end.

figures.title: A view aliases bytes while a copy owns separate storage
figures.description: original and view reference the same backing bytes. view covers indices 1 and 2, now 99 and 30. snapshot references an independent copy containing 20 and 30.

figures.title: Valid bytes and handle release are separate obligations
figures.description: Example B opens a handle and reads at file position 3. bytesRead is 2, exposing de from capacity deXXXXXX. Normal and simulated consumer-failure paths both attempt close in finally.

figures.title: Pressure follows admission of the current chunk
figures.description: On the successful pressure path the chunk is admitted before false is returned. The producer pauses new writes and resumes with the next chunk after drain. Error or premature close stops this path.

figures.title: The signal target determines cancellation scope
figures.description: Aborting finished cancels its observation while the stream stays live for its owner. Aborting pipeline requests destruction of its participating streams; cooperative custom work must still clean up.

figures.title: Different API families contend for one native resource
figures.description: Async PBKDF2 and filesystem requests use the process shared libuv pool. Their native completions return to their associated JavaScript loop. Timer callbacks use loop scheduling rather than consuming one pool worker per timer.

figures.title: Clone transfer and share create different ownership relationships
figures.description: Clone produces independent receiver bytes. Transfer moves a dedicated ArrayBuffer and detaches every sender view. SharedArrayBuffer permits both threads to access the same region with an explicit synchronization protocol.

figures.title: Local IPC sending and child task completion differ
figures.description: The child reports ready, the parent sends task-1, and send returns a local flow-control result. A later child message reports task-1 total 5. Parent and child are separate processes with deserialized data.

figures.title: URL identity controls reuse in the ESM cache fixture
figures.description: Two imports of counter.mjs use the same module record with count 1. Importing counter.mjs with query variant=1 uses another record with count 2 in this sequential fixture.

figures.title: Memory counters are overlapping observations
figures.description: arrayBuffers is included in external. V8 heap counters describe managed memory. RSS observes resident pages across the process and is not another disjoint allocation bucket.

figures.title: Unneeded data can remain reachable
figures.description: A global retaining root keeps the object graph reachable. Removing its last retaining path makes that graph eligible for collection. Collection and release of resident pages to the OS are later distinct events.

figures.title: Invocation context differs from registration context
figures.description: Example B registers both listeners under A. Later emit outside A invokes the plain listener with no store, while the bound wrapper restores captured context A. After either call the outer context is restored.

figures.title: Draining and forced cutoff are different outcomes
figures.description: Ready service enters Draining after a handled stop trigger and admission is stopped. Completed owned work and cleanup permit local closure. A drain deadline can instead lead to forced cutoff with unfinished or unknown outcomes.

figures.title: A blocked loop can consume little parent CPU
figures.description: During spawnSync the parent loop cannot dispatch callbacks and stays outside its event provider. ELU can be near 1 while the parent mostly waits for the separate child, consuming little parent CPU.
